method: Fresh page retrieval in this session; claims below are limited to text visible on the cited official/trusted page. This is source verification, not a leaderboard receipt or a substitute for pinned input bytes.

verified_lines: The task is to predict structures indicative of geothermal resources, namely geological faults.
The public known-fault set is incomplete and may contain inaccurate data; expert-labelled new faults form the test data.
Provided features include surface conductivity, detrended elevation/slope, geodetic strain, gravity, magnetic layers, and earthquake density.
The distance-weighted Tversky kernel has 300 m support (3 pixels at 100 m), with alpha=0.2 and beta=0.8.
Submission format is a single-layer float32 GeoTIFF in EPSG:32611 at 100 m with values from 0 to 1; outside bounds is null or NaN on the official page.
irregularities: The repository's conservative local export policy uses finite zero outside the footprint so its local validators can audit the whole array. That is an implementation policy, not a claim that the portal treats zero and null identically.
The competition page describes public/private and expanded expert labels; this repository has no organizer receipt and cannot infer a live score from local holdout values.

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy / National Laboratory of the Rockies, GEMS Prize Official Rules, September 2026
verified_lines: Section 1.1 describes Phase 1 as a private withheld subset and Phase 2 as an expert-updated label set.
Section 3.3 says training includes a multiband GeoTIFF at 100 m and training fault labels, and submissions are predictions for all faults as a 100 m GeoTIFF.
Section 3.4 says up to three submissions per week may be used for feedback and only one final submission is selected across the prize phases.
Section 3.5 says the submission is automatically evaluated with the distance-weighted Tversky index and final selection must be made without private-test knowledge.
Section 3.2 requires disclosure of generative-AI use in the narrative and states finalists must provide reproducible code assets and documentation.
irregularities: The current repo status is not a rules interpretation that authorizes an upload; it is a stricter internal scientific and registry gate.

sources.publisher: Great Basin Center for Geothermal Energy
verified_lines: The page identifies INGENIOUS and its goal of finding hidden geothermal systems while reducing exploration/development risk.
It lists USGS, state surveys, NREL, LBNL and other collaborators.
It describes an integrated regional-to-prospect workflow including geophysics, geostatistics, play-fairway work and detailed conceptual models.
It links publications and related datasets, including heat flow, regional gravity/magnetics, MT conductance, slip/dilation tendency, and geodetic strain.
irregularities: The page is a project description, not a guarantee that every linked layer is available, co-registered, licensed for this competition, or present in this checkout.

sources.publisher: DOE Geothermal Data Repository / GBCGE / NBMG / UNR
verified_lines: The page identifies the INGENIOUS Great Basin Regional Dataset Compilation and its DOI.
It lists earthquake density, geodetic shear/dilation, geophysics, heat flow, conductance, faults, volcanics, paleo-geothermal features, wells/springs and geochemistry resources.
It labels the dataset publicly accessible and CC BY 4.0, and gives a terms-of-use disclaimer that users must assess fitness.
The page identifies a downloadable earthquake-density archive and separate resource links, but this session did not use those external bytes in a candidate.
irregularities: The GDR page is a catalog/resource page; no external GDR file was promoted into the shared feature stack here. GDR point layers are not a substitute for the required blind holdout.
The repository explicitly excludes any label-derived distance-to-known-fault field from model features.

verified_lines: EPSG:32611 is WGS 84 / UTM zone 11N.
The unit is metre, the coordinate axes are easting/northing, and the listed area is between 120 W and 114 W in the northern hemisphere.
irregularities: The local sample and validator are the authoritative byte/grid pins for this checkout; the EPSG page is a CRS reference, not the competition portal.
